text:
Jordan: quick sync — noticed a spike in rollbacks after the last penalty schedule push to edge regions, looks correlated with probe failures on cold GPUs :thinking:
Maria: ugh, timeline? which schedule/version pushed?
Jordan: rolled v2.4.1 around 15:10 UTC (small TTL tweak + steeper decay). probes started failing ~15:12, rollback triggers at 15:18
Sam: do we have probe sampling jittering? cold gpus + tight probe windows can cause false positives
Maria: yes we do, our probe sampler uses fixed windows and a static retry count. cold instances sometimes drop first few tail probes
Jordan: thought: add a short grace window to schedule activation and treat initial probe errors as "warming" not immediate failures
Sam: makes sense. also maybe add a versioned activation flag in the policy store so we can disable an activation without full rollback
Maria: how about: activation_state: {version: "v2.4.1", staged_until: 1715556000, grace_probes: 3} and the runtime uses staged_until OR observed_success_count to flip active
Jordan: sample config I sketched:
```
penalty_schedule:
  version: "v2.4.1"
  staged_until: 1715556000
  grace_probes: 3
  windows:
    - duration: 60
      weight: 1.5
      decay: 0.92
```
Sam: that helps ops, but we need compile/runtime boundary clarity — compiler should emit hints (staged_until, grace_probes) but runtime must still be authoritative and resilient to clock drift
Maria: agree. Also add telemetry tags to penalty events so we can filter by schedule version in traces (very helpful for postmortem)
Jordan: +1. Another thought: instead of immediate rollback triggers, queue a soft-degrade that reduces weight gradually while sending an alert. Full rollback only if soft-degrade doesn't recover in X minutes
Sam: that reduces flapping. We should also limit how many concurrent schedule activations per region to avoid cascading probe floods
Maria: per-tenant limits too. A noisy tenant deploying many schedules can trigger global noise
Jordan: deploy-bot: started canary rollout for penalty-schedule v2.4.2 -> regions: us-east-1 (10%), eu-west-1 (5%) :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary monitors: probe_success, tail_latency_95, rollback_triggers
Sam: when can we test the staged_until flow? I can wire a quick simulation harness against the policy sandbox
Maria: do that. let's also add a debugging endpoint: `GET /policy-status?version=v2.4.1&region=us-east-1` that returns activation_state + recent probe history (obfuscated)
Jordan: sounds good. I'll open a follow-up RFC for the activation-state contract and runtime guardrails — will include the telemetry keys and the suggested config schema
Maria: assign to Sam for sandbox instrumentation, Jordan for RFC text. I'll add ops checklist for canary monitoring and thresholds
Sam: will do. thanks team
Jordan: thanks — aim to push v2.4.2 with staged activation tomorrow, but hold on global rollout until sandbox signals pass
Maria: :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary healthcheck: us-east-1 metrics stable for 2m, eu-west-1 pending
Sam: leaving some probe jitter in staging to validate grace_probes behavior
Jordan: perfect. closing this thread and tracking in the RFC PR
Maria: noted, will follow PR comments
